When these scientists were born.Galileo Galilei: In 1610 he pointed a telescope at Jupiter and spotted four moons, now called the Galilean moons, proving not everything orbits Earth.
When these scientists were born.Isaac Newton: Newton was born on Christmas Day 1642 by the old Julian calendar, which is why some books give 1642 instead.
When these scientists were born.Antoine Lavoisier: He named oxygen and hydrogen and showed that mass is conserved in reactions, but was guillotined during the French Revolution.
When these scientists were born.Michael Faraday: Faraday left school at 13 and became a bookbinder's apprentice, yet discovered electromagnetic induction, the principle behind generators.
When these scientists were born.James Clerk Maxwell: He unified electricity, magnetism and light in four equations, and also helped produce the first color photograph in 1861.
When these scientists were born.Marie Curie: The only person to win Nobels in two different sciences, physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911, Curie coined the term radioactivity.
When these scientists were born.Albert Einstein: His Nobel Prize was for explaining the photoelectric effect, not for relativity, which the committee considered still too uncertain.
When these scientists were born.Niels Bohr: His model of the atom put electrons in fixed shells, and the element bohrium is named in his honor.
When these scientists were born.Richard Feynman: Feynman's simple diagrams revolutionised particle physics, and on the Challenger inquiry he dunked an O-ring in ice water on live TV.
When these scientists were born.Stephen Hawking: Told he had only a few years after an ALS diagnosis at 21, he lived to 76 and showed that black holes should glow with faint radiation.

Letters in the alphabet.Rotokas: Spoken in Papua New Guinea, this language has the shortest alphabet in the world, just twelve letters.
Letters in the alphabet.Hawaiian: Its alphabet has five vowels, seven consonants and the okina, a glottal stop that is counted as a letter.
Letters in the alphabet.Italian: Italian skips J, K, W, X and Y in native words and keeps them for borrowed words like jeans and whisky.
Letters in the alphabet.Greek: The Greeks borrowed Phoenician letters and added vowels, and the word alphabet comes from the first two, alpha and beta.
Letters in the alphabet.English: The letter E is the most common, and an old tradition once tacked the ampersand on after Z when reciting the alphabet.
Letters in the alphabet.Spanish: Spanish counts the letter ene with a tilde, and in 2010 the Royal Academy stopped treating CH and LL as separate letters.
Letters in the alphabet.Russian: Named for Saint Cyril, Cyrillic here has 33 letters, including two that make no sound of their own and just modify others.
Letters in the alphabet.Armenian: Created around 405 AD by the monk Mesrop Mashtots, the alphabet has stayed largely unchanged for over 1,600 years.
Letters in the alphabet.Japanese hiragana: Its 46 characters developed from cursive Chinese, and in the Heian court women used it for writing, giving it the nickname women's hand.
Letters in the alphabet.Khmer: Cambodia's script is often cited as the longest alphabet in the world, with many consonant and vowel signs.

DreamWorks Animation films by release.Antz: DreamWorks' first release, it starred Woody Allen as a neurotic worker ant, and reached cinemas weeks before Pixar's A Bug's Life.
DreamWorks Animation films by release.Shrek: It won the first Best Animated Feature Oscar, and Mike Myers redid the hero's voice with a Scottish accent.
DreamWorks Animation films by release.Madagascar: Its lemur King Julien became a breakout star, though real lemurs live only on Madagascar and nearby islands.
DreamWorks Animation films by release.Kung Fu Panda: Each of the Furious Five's fighting styles, such as tiger, crane and mantis, echoes a real Chinese martial arts animal style.
DreamWorks Animation films by release.How to Train Your Dragon: Based on Cressida Cowell's books, it gave Toothless a design inspired partly by cats' movements and expressions.
DreamWorks Animation films by release.Puss in Boots: The swashbuckling cat first appeared in Shrek 2, voiced by Antonio Banderas, and starred again in the Oscar-nominated The Last Wish in 2022.
DreamWorks Animation films by release.The Croods: This prehistoric-family comedy cast Nicolas Cage as the overprotective dad Grug, and it spawned a 2020 sequel.
DreamWorks Animation films by release.Trolls: Based on Danish Good Luck Trolls made by Thomas Dam in 1959. Justin Timberlake's 'Can't Stop the Feeling' was nominated for an Oscar.
DreamWorks Animation films by release.The Bad Guys: Based on Aaron Blabey's picture books, the film borrowed a hand-drawn comic look in its 3D animation.
DreamWorks Animation films by release.The Wild Robot: Based on Peter Brown's novel, its painterly style won acclaim and Oscar nominations, including Best Animated Feature.

Top speeds in sport.Elite freestyle swimmer: Water is about 800 times denser than air, so even Olympic swimmers are slower than a casual jogger.
Top speeds in sport.Race walker: One foot must always touch the ground and the leg must be straight as it passes under the body, or judges disqualify you.
Top speeds in sport.Elite marathon runner: Eliud Kipchoge held about this pace for two hours in 2019, running a marathon in under two hours in a staged event.
Top speeds in sport.Sprinter at full speed: Usain Bolt reached about 44.7 km/h during his 100 m world record of 9.58 seconds in 2009.
Top speeds in sport.Racehorse at full gallop: Secretariat won the 1973 Belmont Stakes by 31 lengths in a time that still stands as a record for the race.
Top speeds in sport.Ski jumper at takeoff: Jumpers lean forward to fly like a wing, and on ski-flying hills the record is over 250 m.
Top speeds in sport.Downhill skier: On the Streif at Kitzbühel, the most famous World Cup downhill, racers get close to 140 km/h.
Top speeds in sport.Skydiver in freefall: Belly-down freefall tops out near this speed, and Felix Baumgartner broke the sound barrier jumping from 39 km up in 2012.
Top speeds in sport.F1 car flat out: Its downforce is so strong that, in theory, the car could drive upside down on a tunnel ceiling at high speed.
Top speeds in sport.Top Fuel dragster: It covers 1,000 feet in under four seconds, with a nitromethane-fed engine making over 10,000 horsepower.

First spacecraft to orbit each world.The Moon: It was the first craft to orbit another world, and it reportedly broadcast The Internationale back to Earth.
First spacecraft to orbit each world.Mars: It arrived to find a global dust storm and waited weeks for the dust to clear before mapping.
First spacecraft to orbit each world.Venus: It orbited, and its lander sent the first pictures ever taken from the surface of another planet's surface, Venus.
First spacecraft to orbit each world.Jupiter: Galileo spent eight years studying the planet and moons, and dropped a probe into Jupiter's atmosphere.
First spacecraft to orbit each world.Asteroid Eros: NEAR Shoemaker orbited Eros and then, though not designed to land, touched down on it in 2001.
First spacecraft to orbit each world.Saturn: Cassini studied Saturn for 13 years and carried the Huygens probe to Titan before diving into the planet in 2017.
First spacecraft to orbit each world.Mercury: MESSENGER found evidence of water ice in polar craters, and crashed into the surface in 2015 when its fuel ran out.
First spacecraft to orbit each world.Comet 67P: Rosetta carried the Philae lander, which bounced after touching down and made the first landing on a comet.
First spacecraft to orbit each world.Ceres: Dawn had visited Vesta first, making it the first craft to orbit two bodies beyond Earth, and found bright spots on Ceres.
First spacecraft to orbit each world.Asteroid Bennu: OSIRIS-REx collected a sample and returned about 120 g of it to Earth in 2023.

How long these keep when stored properly.Raw ground beef (fridge): More surface area means more places for bacteria to grow, which is why ground meat spoils faster than a steak.
How long these keep when stored properly.Cooked leftovers (fridge): Reheat leftovers to 74 °C (165 °F) to be safe, and always within about four days.
How long these keep when stored properly.Opened milk (fridge): Pasteurization kills harmful germs but not all spoilage bacteria, so it eventually sours.
How long these keep when stored properly.Raw eggs in shell (fridge): US eggs are washed and refrigerated, but in Europe they are left unwashed and unrefrigerated.
How long these keep when stored properly.Opened mayo (fridge): Store-bought mayonnaise is acidic and made with pasteurized eggs, so it is actually safer than homemade.
How long these keep when stored properly.Opened ketchup (fridge): Vinegar and tomato acidity make it a hostile environment for microbes.
How long these keep when stored properly.Whole chicken (freezer): Frozen at -18 °C, food is technically safe indefinitely, though quality declines.
How long these keep when stored properly.Dried pasta (pantry): Dryness starves microbes, so the date on the bag is about quality, not safety.
How long these keep when stored properly.White rice, sealed (pantry): Stored sealed away from oxygen and warmth, it lasts decades, while brown rice goes rancid within months.
How long these keep when stored properly.Honey: Its low moisture and acidity block microbes, and ancient jars in Egyptian tombs are said to be still edible.

Units of volume.Cubic inch: US engine sizes were given in these, as in a '350 cubic-inch V8'.
Units of volume.Litre: Defined as one cubic decimetre; the name comes from the French litron.
Units of volume.US gallon: Smaller than the imperial gallon (4.55 L); it traces back to the 18th-century English wine gallon.
Units of volume.Cubic foot: Fridge capacity is often quoted in this unit, and a typical one holds 15 to 25 of them.
Units of volume.US bushel: Originally a dry measure for grain, it equals eight gallons.
Units of volume.Barrel of oil: It holds 42 US gallons, a size inherited from old English barrels, and it is still how oil is priced.
Units of volume.Cubic yard: Concrete and soil are sold by this; a mixer truck carries about ten of them.
Units of volume.Cubic metre: This SI unit holds 1,000 litres of water, which weighs a tonne.
Units of volume.Acre-foot: Water managers use it: one acre of land covered a foot deep, roughly a football field flooded to ankle height.
Units of volume.Olympic pool: Competition pools must be 50 by 25 metres and at least 2 metres deep, which works out to about this much.

When these bridges collapsed.Tay Bridge, Scotland: It collapsed in a storm in December 1879 with a train on it, killing about 75 and inspiring William McGonagall's famously bad poem.
When these bridges collapsed.Quebec Bridge (first): It collapsed in 1907 while under construction, killing 75 workers, many of them Mohawk ironworkers from Kahnawake.
When these bridges collapsed.Tacoma Narrows Bridge: Nicknamed Galloping Gertie, it twisted itself apart in a 40 mph wind, and film of it is still shown in engineering classes.
When these bridges collapsed.Silver Bridge, Ohio River: A single failed eyebar brought it down during rush hour in 1967, killing 46 and leading to US bridge inspection rules.
When these bridges collapsed.Sunshine Skyway, Florida: A freighter hit it in fog and storm in 1980, and a bus plunged into the water, among 35 deaths.
When these bridges collapsed.Hintze Ribeiro, Portugal: It collapsed over the Douro in 2001 killing 59 people, in part because of sand extraction from the riverbed.
When these bridges collapsed.I-35W, Minneapolis: It fell during rush hour in 2007, killing 13; investigators traced the failure to undersized gusset plates.
When these bridges collapsed.Morandi Bridge, Genoa: The motorway viaduct fell in 2018, killing 43, and was replaced by a new bridge designed by Renzo Piano.
When these bridges collapsed.Fern Hollow, Pittsburgh: It fell in January 2022 just hours before President Biden arrived to talk about infrastructure; luckily nobody died.
When these bridges collapsed.Francis Scott Key, Baltimore: A container ship lost power and hit it in March 2024, killing six workers who were repairing potholes.

Points from one scoring feat.Basketball free throw: Players shoot from 15 feet, and Rick Barry's old-fashioned underhand shot helped him hit about 90 percent in his career.
Points from one scoring feat.NFL safety: A safety is scored when a team tackles an opponent in their own end zone, and the scoring team also gets the ball back.
Points from one scoring feat.NBA three-pointer: The NBA adopted the three-point line in 1979, and the first one was made by Boston's Chris Ford.
Points from one scoring feat.Rugby union try: It is called a try because it once only earned the right to try for a goal kick, and the player must ground the ball.
Points from one scoring feat.NFL touchdown: A touchdown was worth just a few points in football's early days, and it reached six in 1912.
Points from one scoring feat.Potting the black (snooker): The black is the most valuable ball, and a 147 break requires potting it after each of 15 reds.
Points from one scoring feat.Archery inner gold ring: At 70 metres, Olympic archers aim at a target 122 centimetres across whose 10-point ring is only about 12 centimetres wide.
Points from one scoring feat.Winning an F1 Grand Prix: Winners score 25 under today's system, which began in 2010; before that, a win was worth 10.
Points from one scoring feat.Snooker maximum break: A 147 needs 15 reds with blacks and then all six colours, and Joe Davis made the first official one in 1955.
Points from one scoring feat.Perfect game in bowling: Perfect means twelve consecutive strikes, with 300 the cap because the tenth frame gives two bonus balls.

Household items by weight.Paperclip: During World War II, Norwegians wore paperclips on their lapels as a symbol of unity against the occupation.
Household items by weight.Sheet of printer paper: Paper weight is set in grams per square metre, and an A4 sheet of 80 gsm weighs about five grams.
Household items by weight.AA battery: These batteries are 1.5 volts, while rechargeable ones are nominally 1.2.
Household items by weight.Deck of playing cards: There are 52 factorial possible orderings, so a well-shuffled deck is almost surely in an order never seen before.
Household items by weight.Smartphone: One is more powerful than the computers that guided Apollo to the Moon.
Household items by weight.Bag of sugar: Until 2019 the kilogram was defined by a platinum-iridium cylinder in Paris, then redefined by a fundamental constant.
Household items by weight.House brick: Bricks are among the oldest manufactured building materials, and fired ones date back some 5,000 years.
Household items by weight.Microwave oven: It heats food by making water molecules vibrate, which is why dry items heat poorly.
Household items by weight.Fridge-freezer: It works by moving heat out, and a modern one uses far less electricity than one made decades ago.
Household items by weight.Grand piano: A concert grand has over 200 strings and around 12,000 parts, and the string tension totals about 20 tons.

The Hawaiian alphabet, in its traditiona.E: E comes second in the Hawaiian alphabet, after A, and the language uses only five vowels and eight consonants.
The Hawaiian alphabet, in its traditiona.I: I is the third letter, and Hawaiian vowels can be long, marked by a macron over them.
The Hawaiian alphabet, in its traditiona.O: O is the fourth letter, and in Hawaiian it is a common word on its own.
The Hawaiian alphabet, in its traditiona.U: U is the fifth and last vowel, and Hawaiian is a language that has many vowels together.
The Hawaiian alphabet, in its traditiona.H: H is the first of the consonants listed, and Hawaiian has just a few consonants.
The Hawaiian alphabet, in its traditiona.K: K is a Hawaiian consonant, and it replaced the 'T' sound in many words found in other Polynesian languages.
The Hawaiian alphabet, in its traditiona.L: L is one of the consonants, and it appears in 'lei', 'luau' and 'aloha'.
The Hawaiian alphabet, in its traditiona.M: M is the ninth letter, and it appears in 'mahalo', meaning thank you.
The Hawaiian alphabet, in its traditiona.P: P is the eleventh letter, and it comes right after the ʻokina, which counts as a consonant.
The Hawaiian alphabet, in its traditiona.W: W is the twelfth letter, and it can sound like 'v' or 'w' depending on the word, as in Hawaiʻi.

When these kitchen gadgets were invented.Papin's pressure cooker: Denis Papin called it a steam digester, and it included a safety valve to stop the vessel exploding.
When these kitchen gadgets were invented.Can opener: Tin cans existed for decades before it; people had to cut them open with a hammer and chisel.
When these kitchen gadgets were invented.Waffle iron patent: Cornelius Swarthout of Troy, New York, patented the first one, a device heated over a stove.
When these kitchen gadgets were invented.Electric toaster: Early ones had no automatic shutoff; the pop-up version came in 1919 from Charles Strite.
When these kitchen gadgets were invented.Electric blender: It was invented for soda fountains by Stephen Poplawski, and Fred Waring helped popularize it.
When these kitchen gadgets were invented.Microwave oven (for sale): Engineer Percy Spencer noticed that a chocolate bar had melted in his pocket near a radar tube.
When these kitchen gadgets were invented.Tefal nonstick pan: Marc Grégoire coated his pans after his wife suggested using the same non-stick coating he had used on fishing gear.
When these kitchen gadgets were invented.Crock-Pot: Based on a bean cooker invented by Irving Naxon, it was sold by Rival and became a 1970s staple.
When these kitchen gadgets were invented.Cuisinart food processor: Carl Sontheimer brought the idea home from a French trade show after seeing the Robot-Coupe.
When these kitchen gadgets were invented.Instant Pot: It was invented by Canadian engineers who had lost tech jobs, and it became a hit on Amazon Prime Day.

Famous road races, by first edition.Boston Marathon: The oldest annual marathon was inspired by the first modern Olympics in 1896, and runs on Patriots' Day.
Famous road races, by first edition.Comrades Marathon: This ultramarathon of about 90 km runs between Durban and Pietermaritzburg, alternating 'up' and 'down' directions.
Famous road races, by first edition.New York City Marathon: The first New York race was held in Central Park in 1970 with 127 starters, and now crosses all five boroughs.
Famous road races, by first edition.Honolulu Marathon: It has no time limit, so walkers and runners can finish at their own pace, and the finish is on a Waikiki beachfront.
Famous road races, by first edition.Berlin Marathon: The flat, fast course has produced many world records, and the race starts and finishes near the Brandenburg Gate.
Famous road races, by first edition.Paris Marathon: It starts on the Champs-Élysées and runs through the Bois de Boulogne, passing some of Paris's best-known landmarks.
Famous road races, by first edition.Chicago Marathon: Kelvin Kiptum's 2:00:35 here in 2023 was the fastest marathon ever recorded.
Famous road races, by first edition.London Marathon: Chris Brasher and John Disley founded it after running New York's race, and runners often wear costumes.
Famous road races, by first edition.Los Angeles Marathon: The course runs from Dodger Stadium to the beach at Santa Monica, which gives it the nickname 'Stadium to the Sea'.
Famous road races, by first edition.Tokyo Marathon: Tokyo joined the World Marathon Majors in 2013, becoming the first Asian race in the elite group of six.

Hebrew months, starting from Rosh Hashan.Tishrei: The month of Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Sukkot; the Jewish year turns over here, though the Torah counts it as the seventh month.
Hebrew months, starting from Rosh Hashan.Cheshvan: Also called Marcheshvan, it has no holidays at all, which is why folk tradition calls it 'bitter' (mar) Cheshvan.
Hebrew months, starting from Rosh Hashan.Kislev: The month of Hanukkah, which begins on its 25th day, with its candles lit in the darkest weeks of the year.
Hebrew months, starting from Rosh Hashan.Tevet: The last days of Hanukkah sometimes fall in this month, which is also marked by the fast of the 10th of Tevet.
Hebrew months, starting from Rosh Hashan.Shevat: It holds Tu BiShvat, the new year of the trees, when people eat fruit and plant saplings.
Hebrew months, starting from Rosh Hashan.Adar: Purim falls in this month, which has a saying that joy increases when it begins; leap years add a second one.
Hebrew months, starting from Rosh Hashan.Nisan: The Torah calls it the first month for counting the months, and it holds Passover, which marks the exodus from Egypt.
Hebrew months, starting from Rosh Hashan.Sivan: Its sixth day is Shavuot, the holiday that marks the giving of the Torah and the early wheat harvest.
Hebrew months, starting from Rosh Hashan.Tammuz: Its 17th begins three weeks of mourning before Tisha B'Av, and the month's name comes from Babylonian.
Hebrew months, starting from Rosh Hashan.Elul: A month of reflection before Rosh Hashanah, in which the shofar is sounded each morning to prompt repentance.

When these screen cars first appeared.Adam West's Batmobile: It was built by George Barris from a 1955 Lincoln Futura concept car.
When these screen cars first appeared.Herbie, The Love Bug: This Volkswagen Beetle, with race number 53, drives itself and has a personality of its own.
When these screen cars first appeared.The Mystery Machine: Scooby-Doo's psychedelic van carried the gang on adventures from the late 1960s onward.
When these screen cars first appeared.The General Lee: A Dodge Charger with a Confederate flag on its roof, hundreds of cars were wrecked while filming The Dukes of Hazzard.
When these screen cars first appeared.KITT, Knight Rider: The talking Pontiac Trans Am was voiced by actor William Daniels.
When these screen cars first appeared.Ecto-1, Ghostbusters: A converted 1959 Cadillac ambulance-hearse, it carried the Ghostbusters and their proton packs.
When these screen cars first appeared.Back to the Future DeLorean: The real DMC-12's stainless steel body was brushed metal, and the company collapsed soon after.
When these screen cars first appeared.Fast and Furious Supra: An orange Toyota Supra Mk IV, driven by Brian O'Conner, it revived the model's popularity.
When these screen cars first appeared.Lightning McQueen: Pixar's Cars star wears number 95, a nod to the year Toy Story was released.
When these screen cars first appeared.Bumblebee, Transformers: A Chevrolet Camaro in the live-action films, though in the original cartoon he was a Volkswagen Beetle.

Layers of your palm, from outside in.Stratum corneum: You shed thousands of these dead, flattened cells every minute; the layer is thickest on palms and soles.
Layers of your palm, from outside in.Stratum lucidum: This clear, thin layer appears only in thick skin like palms and soles, which is why it is missing from most of the body.
Layers of your palm, from outside in.Stratum granulosum: Cells here fill with granules and release waxy lipids that waterproof the skin before the cells die.
Layers of your palm, from outside in.Stratum spinosum: Under a microscope its cells look spiky because of desmosomes, tiny protein rivets that bind them tightly together.
Layers of your palm, from outside in.Stratum basale: A single row of stem cells keeps dividing here, and a new cell takes about a month to climb to the surface.
Layers of your palm, from outside in.Papillary dermis: Its finger-like ridges push up into the epidermis and shape your fingerprints and palm prints.
Layers of your palm, from outside in.Reticular dermis: A dense mesh of collagen and elastin gives skin its strength and stretch; stretch marks are tears in this layer.
Layers of your palm, from outside in.Subcutaneous fat: Pads of fat in the palm and fingertips act as shock absorbers when you grip or strike.
Layers of your palm, from outside in.Muscle: Most of your grip power comes from forearm muscles, whose long tendons run through the carpal tunnel to the fingers.
Layers of your palm, from outside in.Bone: Each hand has 27 bones, so your two hands hold more than a quarter of all the bones in your body.

Landmark moments in medicine.Vesalius's anatomy book: De humani corporis fabrica, built on his own dissections, corrected centuries of Galen's errors.
Landmark moments in medicine.Harvey explains circulation: William Harvey showed that blood circulates, pumped by the heart, rather than being consumed by tissues.
Landmark moments in medicine.Jenner's smallpox vaccine: He used cowpox from a milkmaid to protect James Phipps, eight, and the word vaccine comes from vacca, Latin for cow.
Landmark moments in medicine.Ether anesthesia demo: It happened in the Ether Dome of Massachusetts General Hospital, still standing; dentist William Morton gave the ether.
Landmark moments in medicine.Lister's antiseptic surgery: He used carbolic acid spray and death rates fell; Listerine is named in his honor.
Landmark moments in medicine.Röntgen discovers X-rays: He X-rayed his wife Anna's hand, and she reportedly said she had seen her own death; he won the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.
Landmark moments in medicine.Fleming finds penicillin: He found mold killing bacteria in a forgotten dish, and Florey and Chain made it into a drug a decade later.
Landmark moments in medicine.First human heart transplant: Christiaan Barnard operated in Cape Town, and patient Louis Washkansky lived 18 days.
Landmark moments in medicine.Smallpox declared eradicated: It is the only human disease declared eradicated; its last natural case was in Somalia in 1977.
Landmark moments in medicine.Human Genome Project done: It took 13 years and about $3 billion to sequence roughly 3 billion DNA letters.

Musical intervals by size.Minor second: The two-note 'Jaws' theme is this interval, the most dissonant step, and it spans the notes E and F.
Musical intervals by size.Major second: A whole tone, the first step of a major scale; 'Frère Jacques' starts with do-re-mi.
Musical intervals by size.Minor third: Often called the 'sad' interval, it opens 'Greensleeves' and 'Smoke on the Water'.
Musical intervals by size.Major third: This interval makes a chord sound major, and it begins 'When the Saints Go Marching In'.
Musical intervals by size.Perfect fourth: It opens 'Here Comes the Bride', and a fourth is the gap between the first two notes.
Musical intervals by size.Tritone: Once called 'diabolus in musica', the devil in music, and it opens 'Maria' from West Side Story.
Musical intervals by size.Perfect fifth: The Star Wars main theme begins with this interval, and it underlies much of music tuning.
Musical intervals by size.Minor sixth: The theme from 'Love Story' opens with this wistful leap.
Musical intervals by size.Major sixth: 'My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean' begins with this upward leap.
Musical intervals by size.Octave: Same note name, double the frequency; 'Somewhere Over the Rainbow' begins with a leap this size.

US cities from west to east.Honolulu: The only royal palace on US soil, Iolani Palace, stands here, and Pearl Harbor is close.
US cities from west to east.Anchorage: Alaska's biggest city holds about 40 percent of the state's population, and moose wander its streets.
US cities from west to east.Seattle: Boeing's hometown and base for Amazon and Starbucks; the Space Needle was built for the 1962 World's Fair.
US cities from west to east.Phoenix: Named for the mythical bird rising from the ashes of an ancient Hohokam canal civilization.
US cities from west to east.Denver: It sits at exactly one mile above sea level, and a step at the state Capitol marks the spot.
US cities from west to east.Dallas: President Kennedy was assassinated here in 1963, and Texas Instruments, which built the first integrated circuit, is based here.
US cities from west to east.Chicago: Nicknamed the Windy City, and its river was reversed in 1900 so sewage would flow away from the lake.
US cities from west to east.Indianapolis: It hosts the Indy 500 each Memorial Day weekend at a speedway nicknamed the Brickyard.
It isn't a state; Pierre L'Enfant designed it on land donated by Maryland and Virginia.
US cities from west to east.Boston: Founded in 1630, it has the Freedom Trail through Revolutionary sites and hosts the world's oldest annual marathon.

Arctic and North Atlantic islands by are.Jan Mayen: This volcanic Norwegian island has no permanent residents, only weather station and military staff. Its Beerenberg volcano rises over 2,200 m.
Arctic and North Atlantic islands by are.Wrangel Island: A Russian Arctic island that was a refuge for woolly mammoths; they survived there until about 4,000 years ago, long after mainland ones vanished.
Arctic and North Atlantic islands by are.Spitsbergen: The main island of Svalbard hosts the town of Longyearbyen. Here the Global Seed Vault stores backup crop seeds deep in the permafrost.
Arctic and North Atlantic islands by are.Devon Island: The largest uninhabited island on Earth. Its Haughton crater, made by an impact, is used by NASA as a Mars analog.
Arctic and North Atlantic islands by are.Banks Island: Home to Sachs Harbour, its only village, and to one of the densest muskox populations on Earth, thousands of them roaming the tundra.
Arctic and North Atlantic islands by are.Iceland: Sitting on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, it is volcanically active and geothermally heated. Glaciers such as Vatnajokull cover roughly a tenth of the country.
Arctic and North Atlantic islands by are.Ellesmere Island: Canada's northernmost large island, with Alert, the world's northernmost permanently inhabited place, near its tip. Parts are a polar desert.
Arctic and North Atlantic islands by are.Victoria Island: One of the biggest islands on Earth, it is shared by Nunavut and the Northwest Territories, and its Cambridge Bay is the largest community.
Arctic and North Atlantic islands by are.Baffin Island: Fifth largest island in the world. Its name is said to honor the explorer William Baffin, and its Inuit community of Iqaluit is the capital of Nunavut.
Arctic and North Atlantic islands by are.Greenland: The world's largest island that is not a continent. Its ice sheet is up to about 3 km thick and holds enough water to raise sea levels by roughly 7 meters.

Surface gravity: where would you feel he.Pluto: A dwarf planet with only about 6 percent of Earth's gravity. NASA's New Horizons flew past in 2015 and found a heart-shaped glacier of nitrogen ice.
Surface gravity: where would you feel he.Titan: Saturn's largest moon has a thick nitrogen atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane. With low gravity and dense air, a human could in principle fly with wings strapped on.
Surface gravity: where would you feel he.The Moon: Gravity is only about one sixth of Earth's. On Apollo 14 in 1971, Alan Shepard hit golf balls on the surface, and they flew much farther than on Earth.
Surface gravity: where would you feel he.Io: The most volcanically active body in the solar system, this moon of Jupiter has volcanoes that can spew lava hundreds of kilometers high.
Surface gravity: where would you feel he.Mars: Gravity is about 38 percent of Earth's. Its Olympus Mons is the tallest known volcano in the solar system, about two and a half times the height of Everest.
Surface gravity: where would you feel he.Venus: Venus's gravity is almost like Earth's, at about 90 percent, yet its surface is crushing and hot enough to melt lead.
Surface gravity: where would you feel he.Earth: Standard gravity, 9.8 m/s². It's the baseline, and a fall from a height takes about one second to cover five meters.
Surface gravity: where would you feel he.Neptune: A giant planet with gravity a little above Earth's, despite having 17 times Earth's mass, since its gas surface is far from its center.
Surface gravity: where would you feel he.Jupiter (cloud tops): Gravity here is about 2.5 times Earth's, so a 70 kg person would weigh like 175 kg. It has no solid surface to stand on, though.
Surface gravity: where would you feel he.The Sun (photosphere): A person here would weigh about 28 times as much as on Earth, though the surface is around 5,500 C, so weight would be the least of the problems.

Wingspans: birds, bats and bugs.Fruit fly: The fruit fly is a favorite model organism in genetics, and it has been in many Nobel Prize-winning studies.
Wingspans: birds, bats and bugs.Housefly: Houseflies have sticky pads on their feet, and they taste with their feet.
Wingspans: birds, bats and bugs.Honeybee: Honeybees beat their wings about 200 times a second, and that's what makes their buzz.
Wingspans: birds, bats and bugs.Monarch butterfly: Monarchs migrate thousands of kilometers, and no individual completes the full round trip.
Wingspans: birds, bats and bugs.Atlas moth: This is a wood-fired pizza oven, which runs at roughly this heat and cooks a Neapolitan pizza in about a minute.
Wingspans: birds, bats and bugs.Blue jay: Blue jays can mimic hawk calls, and they bury acorns that become oak seedlings.
Wingspans: birds, bats and bugs.American crow: Crows can recognize human faces, and they may hold grudges for years.
Wingspans: birds, bats and bugs.Golden-crowned flying fox: This bat is among the largest, and it eats fruit and lives in Philippine forests.
Wingspans: birds, bats and bugs.Golden eagle: Golden eagles can dive at over 240 km/h, and they were used in falconry for hunting wolves.
Wingspans: birds, bats and bugs.Andean condor: The Andean condor is one of the largest flying birds, and it can soar for hours without flapping.

Steps of the Passover Seder, in order.Kadesh: bless the wine: The first of four cups of wine drunk during the evening; the name means 'sanctification'.
Steps of the Passover Seder, in order.Karpas: dip greens: Usually parsley or potato dipped in salt water to recall the tears of slavery.
Steps of the Passover Seder, in order.Yachatz: break the matzah: The middle of three matzot is broken, and the larger piece is hidden away to become the afikoman.
Steps of the Passover Seder, in order.Maggid: tell the story: The retelling of the Exodus, which includes the Four Questions traditionally asked by the youngest at the table.
Steps of the Passover Seder, in order.Maror: bitter herbs: Horseradish or romaine lettuce is often used to recall the bitterness of slavery.
Steps of the Passover Seder, in order.Korech: Hillel's sandwich: It is named for Hillel the Elder, the sage who is said to have eaten matzah, bitter herbs and the Passover lamb together.
Steps of the Passover Seder, in order.Shulchan Orech: the meal: The name means 'set table', and many families begin the meal with eggs in salt water.
Steps of the Passover Seder, in order.Tzafun: find the afikoman: The name means 'hidden'; children search for the afikoman, which is the last food eaten.
Steps of the Passover Seder, in order.Barech: grace after meals: The grace after the meal comes with the third cup of wine.
Steps of the Passover Seder, in order.Nirtzah: next year!: The seder ends with 'Next year in Jerusalem', and nirtzah means 'accepted': the service has been completed.

Sound frequencies, from rumble to ultras.Lower limit of human hearing: Below it is infrasound, which elephants and some whales use to talk over very long distances.
Sound frequencies, from rumble to ultras.Lowest piano key: A standard piano has 88 keys, but the Bösendorfer Imperial adds extra bass notes reaching down to about 16 Hz.
Sound frequencies, from rumble to ultras.Typical male speaking voice: At this pitch the vocal folds open and close about 120 times each second.
Sound frequencies, from rumble to ultras.Typical female speaking voice: It is higher mostly because the vocal folds are shorter and lighter, so they vibrate more quickly.
Sound frequencies, from rumble to ultras.Middle C: Doubling a frequency raises a note by one octave, so the C above middle C is roughly 523 Hz.
Sound frequencies, from rumble to ultras.Orchestra tuning A: Baroque ensembles often tune lower, near 415 Hz, so period-instrument performances can sound about a semitone flatter.
Sound frequencies, from rumble to ultras.Highest piano key: Dog whistles lie several times higher than this, and are inaudible to us but clear to dogs.
Sound frequencies, from rumble to ultras.Teens-only mosquito tone: Some shops used this sound to drive away loitering teenagers, because adults' hearing has usually dulled at this height.
Sound frequencies, from rumble to ultras.Upper limit of human hearing: Dogs hear up to about 45 kHz and bats far higher, so a lot of the sound world is silent to us.
Sound frequencies, from rumble to ultras.Medical ultrasound scan: It bounces sound off tissue and times the echoes, building an image without radiation, which is why it's used for pregnancy scans.

When these vaccines first arrived.Smallpox: Edward Jenner used cowpox to protect against a deadly disease that was declared eradicated in 1980, the only human disease wiped out so far.
When these vaccines first arrived.Rabies: Louis Pasteur's first test on a nine-year-old boy bitten by a rabid dog worked, and the boy survived without symptoms.
When these vaccines first arrived.BCG (tuberculosis): The Bacillus Calmette-Guérin vaccine was developed over 13 years of repeated culture, and it is still used in many countries.
When these vaccines first arrived.Yellow fever: Max Theiler won a Nobel Prize for the vaccine against this mosquito-borne virus, developed by weakening the virus in mice and chicken embryos.
When these vaccines first arrived.Polio (Salk): Jonas Salk refused to patent his vaccine, famously asking, 'Could you patent the sun?'
When these vaccines first arrived.Measles: Maurice Hilleman developed it from a virus taken from his own daughter's throat, and the vaccine is now part of a combined shot.
When these vaccines first arrived.Mumps: Hilleman also created this vaccine in 1967, again using a virus taken from his daughter Jeryl Lynn, whose name is on the strain.
When these vaccines first arrived.Hepatitis B: This was the first vaccine to prevent a cancer, since the virus can cause liver cancer, and it was made from the plasma of infected people.
When these vaccines first arrived.HPV: The vaccine protects against a virus that causes most cervical cancers, and it is one of the few vaccines to prevent cancer.
When these vaccines first arrived.COVID-19 mRNA: The first approved vaccines to use messenger RNA were developed in under a year, and the technology led to a Nobel Prize in 2023.

When these famous ships were lost.Mary Rose: Henry VIII's flagship sank off Portsmouth in 1545 and was raised in 1982, a rescue that millions watched on TV.
When these famous ships were lost.Vasa: This Swedish warship sank on its maiden voyage after sailing barely a kilometer and was raised in 1961. It is now a museum.
When these famous ships were lost.RMS Titanic: It hit an iceberg on its maiden voyage, killing about 1,500, and the wreck was found in 1985 by Robert Ballard.
When these famous ships were lost.RMS Lusitania: A German U-boat torpedoed it off Ireland, killing about 1,200 and helping to draw the US into World War I.
When these famous ships were lost.Wilhelm Gustloff: Sunk by a Soviet submarine while carrying refugees, it was the deadliest ship sinking in history.
When these famous ships were lost.Andrea Doria: The Italian liner collided with the Stockholm in fog, and most of the 1,700 aboard were saved.
When these famous ships were lost.Edmund Fitzgerald: This Great Lakes freighter sank in a Lake Superior storm, and Gordon Lightfoot wrote a famous song about it.
When these famous ships were lost.Exxon Valdez runs aground: The tanker spilled about 11 million US gallons of crude into Alaska's Prince William Sound.
When these famous ships were lost.MS Estonia: This Baltic ferry sank after its bow visor failed, and 852 people died.
When these famous ships were lost.Costa Concordia: The cruise ship ran onto rocks off Giglio, Italy, killing 32, and its captain was convicted.

How long ago did they vanish?.Trilobites: These armoured sea creatures had calcite crystal eyes and vanished in the Permian extinction, leaving a rich fossil record.
How long ago did they vanish?.Ichthyosaurs: These dolphin-shaped marine reptiles gave birth to live young in the water, and died out well before the dinosaurs.
How long ago did they vanish?.Non-avian dinosaurs: Birds are living dinosaurs, so strictly speaking only the non-avian kind went extinct.
How long ago did they vanish?.Megalodon: Known mostly from teeth as big as a hand, this giant shark may have been 15 metres long.
How long ago did they vanish?.Neanderthals: Many people today carry one to two percent Neanderthal DNA, thanks to interbreeding with our ancestors.
How long ago did they vanish?.Cave bear: Its skulls fill European caves, and despite its size it was mostly a plant eater.
How long ago did they vanish?.Smilodon: Its fangs reached about 18 cm, and the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles have yielded thousands.
How long ago did they vanish?.Irish elk: Neither Irish nor an elk, this giant deer carried antlers spanning up to about 3.5 metres.
How long ago did they vanish?.Woolly mammoth: A dwarf population lasted until about 4,000 years ago on Wrangel Island, when the pyramids were already ancient.
How long ago did they vanish?.Moa: New Zealand's giant flightless birds were hunted out soon after Polynesian settlers arrived, and Haast's eagle once preyed on them.

Fish on the scale.Guppy: Guppies bear live young instead of laying eggs, and the males' colors vary so much that each is almost unique.
Fish on the scale.Clownfish: Clownfish live among anemone tentacles, immune to their stings; all are born male, and the dominant one becomes female.
Fish on the scale.Goldfish: Goldfish were bred from Chinese carp over a thousand years ago, and their memories last for months, not seconds.
Fish on the scale.Red-bellied piranha: Piranha attacks on people are rare; they mostly eat fish, insects and carrion, and are shy in groups.
Fish on the scale.Atlantic salmon: Salmon return to the river where they hatched to spawn, using smell to navigate hundreds of kilometers back.
Fish on the scale.Mahi-mahi: Mahi-mahi, also called dolphinfish, grow fast and live only a few years, and flash brilliant colors that fade after death.
Fish on the scale.Arapaima: The Amazon's arapaima must regularly gulp air at the surface, because its gills alone can't supply enough oxygen.
Fish on the scale.Atlantic bluefin tuna: A bluefin sold in Tokyo in 2019 for over 3 million dollars, making it the priciest fish ever auctioned.
Fish on the scale.Great white shark: A white shark can sense faint electrical fields with jelly-filled pores in its snout, called ampullae of Lorenzini.
Fish on the scale.Whale shark: The largest fish alive filters plankton, and the pattern of spots on each whale shark is unique, like a fingerprint.

macOS releases named after California pl.Yosemite: Yosemite was the first macOS with the flat, modern look, and it takes its name from a National Park in the Sierra Nevada.
macOS releases named after California pl.El Capitan: El Capitan is a 900 m granite monolith loved by climbers; Alex Honnold climbed it without ropes in 2017.
macOS releases named after California pl.Sierra: Named for the Sierra Nevada range, it was the release that renamed OS X as macOS and brought Siri to the Mac.
macOS releases named after California pl.High Sierra: The name signals a refinement of Sierra, and it introduced the Apple File System, APFS, to the Mac.
macOS releases named after California pl.Mojave: The Mojave Desert gave this version its name, and it brought Dark Mode to the whole system.
macOS releases named after California pl.Catalina: Santa Catalina Island lies off Los Angeles; the version ended iTunes on the Mac and dropped 32-bit apps.
macOS releases named after California pl.Big Sur: Big Sur is a rugged stretch of California coast, and the release was the first numbered 11 and the first to support Apple silicon.
macOS releases named after California pl.Monterey: Monterey, on California's coast, is known for its aquarium; the version brought Shortcuts and Universal Control to the Mac.
macOS releases named after California pl.Ventura: Ventura is a coastal California city and county, and the release introduced Stage Manager for organizing windows.
macOS releases named after California pl.Sonoma: Sonoma is California wine country; the version added desktop widgets and many gaming improvements.

How old were they at their big moment?.Mozart writes his 1st symphony: Mozart wrote his first symphony in London in 1764, on a European tour as a child prodigy with his father and sister.
How old were they at their big moment?.Greta Thunberg's first strike: Greta Thunberg began her school strike for the climate outside the Swedish parliament in August 2018, at age 15, sitting alone.
How old were they at their big moment?.Zuckerberg launches Facebook: Zuckerberg launched thefacebook from his Harvard dorm in February 2004, and it spread first to other universities.
How old were they at their big moment?.Shelley publishes Frankenstein: Mary Shelley began Frankenstein at 18 and published it anonymously in 1818; it is often called the first science fiction novel.
How old were they at their big moment?.Tiger Woods's 1st Masters win: Tiger Woods won the 1997 Masters by 12 strokes, a record margin, becoming its youngest and first Black champion.
How old were they at their big moment?.Usain Bolt runs 9.58: Bolt's 9.58 s in Berlin in 2009 is still the 100 m world record, reaching a top speed of about 44 km/h.
How old were they at their big moment?.Neil Armstrong on the Moon: Armstrong was 38 when he took one small step on July 20, 1969, watched on TV by hundreds of millions.
How old were they at their big moment?.Obama's inauguration: Barack Obama became the 44th president and the first Black president of the United States.
How old were they at their big moment?.Julius Caesar's assassination: Caesar was stabbed by a group of senators on the Ides of March in 44 BC, suffering around 23 wounds, at a meeting of the Senate.
How old were they at their big moment?.Mandela becomes president: Mandela became South Africa's first democratically elected president in 1994, after 27 years in prison.

Unlocking electricity, step by step.Gilbert's De Magnete: William Gilbert, physician to Elizabeth I, coined the word 'electricus' from the Greek for amber and argued Earth is a giant magnet.
Unlocking electricity, step by step.Leyden jar: Invented in Leiden, this glass jar stored static charge; public demos sent shocks through chains of people holding hands.
Unlocking electricity, step by step.Franklin's kite: The kite story links lightning to electricity, though details are debated; others who tried similar tests were killed.
Unlocking electricity, step by step.Galvani's twitching frogs: Luigi Galvani saw dissected frog legs twitch against metal and proposed 'animal electricity', sparking a debate that led to the battery.
Unlocking electricity, step by step.Volta's pile: Alessandro Volta stacked zinc and copper discs separated by brine-soaked card to make the first battery; the volt honours him.
Unlocking electricity, step by step.Ørsted: current moves compass: During a lecture, Hans Christian Ørsted noticed a compass needle twitch near a wire, the first link between electricity and magnetism.
Unlocking electricity, step by step.Faraday's induction: Michael Faraday showed a moving magnet creates current in a coil, the principle behind generators and transformers.
Unlocking electricity, step by step.Maxwell's equations: James Clerk Maxwell unified electricity, magnetism and light, predicting radio waves before anyone detected them.
Unlocking electricity, step by step.Hertz detects radio waves: Heinrich Hertz made and detected radio waves in his lab, proving Maxwell right; the unit of frequency honours him.
Unlocking electricity, step by step.Superconductivity: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes found mercury lost all resistance near minus 269 °C, using liquid helium he had just liquefied.

Caffeine per serving.Cup of decaf coffee: Even decaf has a trace, because removing caffeine is never perfect, and a big cup can still carry a few milligrams.
Caffeine per serving.Milk chocolate bar: Chocolate gets its small caffeine kick from cocoa beans, and it also contains theobromine, which is toxic to dogs.
Caffeine per serving.Can of Coca-Cola: Its famous cola recipe once had cocaine from coca leaves, but today only caffeine remains, in a modest 34 mg per can.
Caffeine per serving.Cup of black tea: The tea plant is the same species for black, green, and white teas, and caffeine content depends mainly on brewing.
Caffeine per serving.Shot of espresso: An espresso shot packs less caffeine than a cup of drip coffee, because it's a much smaller volume, though it is concentrated.
Caffeine per serving.Small can of Red Bull: Its name comes from a Thai tonic, Krating Daeng, meaning 'red bull', and its small can packs a modest amount of caffeine.
Caffeine per serving.Cup of brewed coffee: A typical cup of brewed coffee has about 95 mg, and the amount varies with the bean, roast and brewing time.
Caffeine per serving.Can of Monster (16 oz): A 16-ounce can holds 160 mg, enough that energy drink sales are restricted to adults in some places.
Caffeine per serving.NoDoz tablet: This pill is sold to keep drivers and night owls awake, and one tablet is roughly the caffeine of four cups of tea.
Caffeine per serving.Starbucks Venti brewed: One Venti cup holds roughly the 400 mg that health agencies suggest as the daily limit for most adults, and about five small Red Bulls.

Judges of Israel, in biblical order.Othniel: Caleb's nephew became the first judge, delivering Israel from the king of Aram.
Judges of Israel, in biblical order.Ehud: Left-handed, he killed the Moabite king Eglon with a hidden dagger.
Judges of Israel, in biblical order.Deborah: A prophet who judged Israel under a palm tree and led Barak's army, one of the few women leaders in the Bible.
Judges of Israel, in biblical order.Gideon: He whittled his army to 300, who broke jars and blew trumpets to rout the Midianites.
Judges of Israel, in biblical order.Tola: A minor judge who led Israel for 23 years from Shamir.
Judges of Israel, in biblical order.Jephthah: He swore a vow to sacrifice whoever first greeted him, which turned out to be his daughter.
Judges of Israel, in biblical order.Ibzan: A minor judge from Bethlehem, known for his 30 sons and 30 daughters.
Judges of Israel, in biblical order.Elon: A minor judge from Zebulun who judged for ten years, and about whom little else is told.
Judges of Israel, in biblical order.Abdon: A minor judge known for 40 sons and 30 grandsons riding seventy donkeys.
Judges of Israel, in biblical order.Samson: Famed for strength tied to his uncut hair, he was betrayed by Delilah.

How many does a typical adult have?.Heart chambers: Two upper atria and two lower ventricles beat about 100,000 times a day.
How many does a typical adult have?.Permanent teeth: That count includes wisdom teeth, which many people never grow or have removed.
How many does a typical adult have?.Bones: Babies are born with around 300, and some bones fuse as they grow.
How many does a typical adult have?.Skeletal muscles: The smallest, the stapedius in the ear, is only a few millimetres long.
How many does a typical adult have?.Taste buds: They are replaced every week or two, and they sit not just on your tongue but in your throat as well.
How many does a typical adult have?.Hairs on the head: The number varies by hair colour, with blondes having more and redheads fewer.
How many does a typical adult have?.Sweat glands: Humans are exceptional sweaters among mammals, which may have helped our ancestors run prey down in the heat.
How many does a typical adult have?.Lung alveoli: Spread flat, these tiny air sacs would cover roughly 70 square metres, about the floor area of a small flat.
How many does a typical adult have?.Neurons in the brain: Suzana Herculano-Houzel's 2009 count replaced the old figure of 100 billion with this more careful estimate.
How many does a typical adult have?.Red blood cells: About two million new ones are made every second, and each one lives for around 120 days.

How long can these plants live?.Thale cress (Arabidopsis): Thale cress is a tiny weed that's the lab rat of plant science, and its genome was the first plant genome sequenced.
How long can these plants live?.Sunflower: Sunflowers track the sun when they're young, and the heads of mature plants usually face east.
How long can these plants live?.Carrot: Carrots flower only in their second year, and the orange ones were bred in the Netherlands, hundreds of years ago.
How long can these plants live?.Peach tree: Peach trees originated in China, and they are typically productive for about a dozen years.
How long can these plants live?.Silver birch: Silver birch is often among the first trees to colonize bare ground, and its white bark peels in thin papery layers.
How long can these plants live?.Saguaro cactus: Saguaro cacti grow very slowly, and they might not grow arms until they are about 75 years old.
How long can these plants live?.Sugar maple: Sugar maples give us maple syrup, and it takes about 40 liters of sap to make one liter of syrup.
How long can these plants live?.English oak: English oaks can host hundreds of insect species, and some in Britain are over a thousand years old.
How long can these plants live?.Giant sequoia: Giant sequoias are the most massive trees on Earth, and their thick bark helps them survive fire.
How long can these plants live?.Bristlecone pine: Bristlecone pines in California's White Mountains include individuals about 4,800 years old, among the oldest living things.

The Ten Plagues of Egypt, in order.Water turned to blood: In Exodus the Nile turns to blood, killing fish. Egyptians dug wells for drinking water.
The Ten Plagues of Egypt, in order.Frogs: Frogs overran Egypt, even bedrooms and ovens, in Exodus. Heqet, an Egyptian frog-headed goddess, ruled fertility.
The Ten Plagues of Egypt, in order.Lice: The Egyptian magicians could copy earlier plagues, but not this one. 'Kinnim' is traditionally translated as lice, though some say gnats.
The Ten Plagues of Egypt, in order.Flies: The swarm hit Egyptians but spared Goshen, where the Israelites lived.
The Ten Plagues of Egypt, in order.Livestock die: Disease struck cattle, horses, camels and sheep, perhaps challenging Egypt's animal gods.
The Ten Plagues of Egypt, in order.Boils: Moses tossed ashes into the air, and they became dust causing festering boils on people and beasts.
The Ten Plagues of Egypt, in order.Hail: Hail mixed with fire destroyed flax and barley, but wheat was spared since it ripened later.
The Ten Plagues of Egypt, in order.Locusts: Locusts ate everything left after the hail. Real desert locust swarms can cover hundreds of square kilometres.
The Ten Plagues of Egypt, in order.Darkness: A thick darkness lasted three days, so heavy it could be felt, while the Israelites had light.
The Ten Plagues of Egypt, in order.Death of the firstborn: The origin of Passover, when lamb's blood on doorposts made death 'pass over' Israelite homes.

Ancient Americas, in chronological order.Olmec San Lorenzo flourishes: The Olmec carved giant heads from basalt, some weighing 20 tonnes or more. The stone was hauled many kilometres, without wheels.
Ancient Americas, in chronological order.Chavín de Huántar rises: This temple site in the Peruvian Andes has underground galleries, and stone carvings of fanged beings. It influenced cultures across the Andes.
Ancient Americas, in chronological order.Monte Albán founded: The Zapotecs levelled a mountaintop in Oaxaca for their capital. It flourished for about 1,000 years.
Ancient Americas, in chronological order.Teotihuacan begins to grow: Its Pyramid of the Sun is one of the largest in the Americas. The Aztecs later found the ruins and named it "place where the gods were created."
Ancient Americas, in chronological order.Pakal buried at Palenque: Pakal ruled Palenque for nearly 70 years. His tomb has a famous carved lid, which some fans claim shows an astronaut.
Ancient Americas, in chronological order.Toltec Tula at its peak: The Toltecs left towering stone warrior statues at Tula. The Aztecs later saw them as the great founders of civilisation.
Ancient Americas, in chronological order.Mayapán founded: The last big Maya capital in Yucatan was a walled city. It fell apart in the mid-1400s after a revolt.
Ancient Americas, in chronological order.Tenochtitlan founded: Legend said the Aztecs should build where they saw an eagle on a cactus, and they found it on an island. Mexico City now lies on the site.
Ancient Americas, in chronological order.Pachacuti expands the Inca: This ruler turned a small kingdom around Cusco into the Inca empire. He is often credited with the royal estate of Machu Picchu.
Ancient Americas, in chronological order.Columbus reaches the Americas: Columbus landed in the Bahamas believing he'd reached Asia. Millions of people had lived in the Americas for thousands of years.

When these great thinkers were born.Thales: Considered the first Western philosopher, he said everything was made of water. He is also said to have predicted an eclipse.
When these great thinkers were born.Confucius: His teachings were collected in the Analects. His ideas on respect and family have shaped East Asia for 2,500 years.
When these great thinkers were born.Socrates: He wrote nothing himself, and we know him from students like Plato. He was sentenced to death by drinking hemlock.
When these great thinkers were born.Plato: Plato founded the Academy in Athens, one of the first universities. His Republic describes an ideal city ruled by philosophers.
When these great thinkers were born.Aristotle: Aristotle tutored a young Alexander the Great. He wrote on everything from logic to biology, and founded the Lyceum.
When these great thinkers were born.Epicurus: He taught in a garden in Athens that pleasure meant peace of mind, not luxury. Epicureans were fond of simple food and friends.
When these great thinkers were born.Seneca: A Roman Stoic, he tutored the young Nero. Nero later ordered him to take his own life.
When these great thinkers were born.Marcus Aurelius: The Roman emperor wrote his Meditations as private notes to himself. He wrote them partly during military campaigns.
When these great thinkers were born.Augustine of Hippo: The bishop of Hippo, in North Africa, wrote Confessions, an early autobiography. His ideas strongly shaped Western Christianity.
When these great thinkers were born.Thomas Aquinas: This Italian friar's Summa Theologica blended Aristotle with Christian faith. His classmates nicknamed him the "Dumb Ox."

Writing tools through history.Clay tablet and stylus: Sumerians pressed wedge-shaped marks into wet clay, creating cuneiform; the name comes from Latin 'cuneus', meaning wedge.
Writing tools through history.Paper: Traditionally credited to Cai Lun, a Chinese court official, who used tree bark, rags and old fishnets.
Writing tools through history.Quill pen: Usually a goose feather, it ruled writing for about a thousand years; 'pen' comes from Latin 'penna', a feather.
Writing tools through history.Graphite pencil: A huge graphite deposit at Borrowdale in England led to the first pencils; the 'lead' in them contains no lead.
Writing tools through history.Pencil with eraser tip: Hymen Lipman patented fitting an eraser to a pencil end in 1858, but the patent was later thrown out.
Writing tools through history.Typewriter: Christopher Latham Sholes's design introduced the QWERTY layout, often said to reduce key jams.
Writing tools through history.Waterman fountain pen: Legend says Lewis Waterman invented his reliable pen after a leaky one ruined a sales contract.
Writing tools through history.Ballpoint pen: Hungarian journalist László Bíró saw how fast newspaper ink dried; in Britain such pens are still called biros.
Writing tools through history.Liquid Paper: Secretary Bette Nesmith Graham first mixed it in her kitchen; her son Michael was a member of The Monkees.
Writing tools through history.Felt-tip pen: Invented in Japan in 1962, it used a fibre tip to hold ink, and today's markers descend from it.

A swallow's year, step by step.Arrives back in spring: Swallows arrive in Britain around April after flying 10,000 km or more from Africa. The saying goes that one swallow does not make a summer.
A swallow's year, step by step.Repairs its mud nest: Swallows use mud pellets mixed with grass, and may reuse the same nest for years. They often nest in barns and under eaves.
A swallow's year, step by step.Lays eggs: A female lays a clutch of about four or five white eggs speckled with red. Many pairs will raise two or three broods a year.
A swallow's year, step by step.Sits on the eggs: The female does most of the incubating over about two weeks. Both parents stay close to the nest, and defend it from intruders.
A swallow's year, step by step.Chicks hatch: Newly hatched chicks are tiny and naked, and their mouths are bright yellow-rimmed to show parents where to drop food.
A swallow's year, step by step.Parents feed them insects: The parents catch flies in flight and bring them back to the nest. A pair can make hundreds of feeding trips a day.
A swallow's year, step by step.Chicks leave the nest: Young swallows fledge after about three weeks. The parents keep feeding them for a while, sometimes even in mid-air.
A swallow's year, step by step.Flocks gather on wires: In late summer swallows line up on wires and roofs, preparing for migration. These gatherings are a sign that autumn is near.
A swallow's year, step by step.Flies south: They travel by day, feeding as they fly, and cross the Sahara. Ringing studies show some individuals make this trip year after year.
A swallow's year, step by step.Spends winter in Africa: British swallows winter mostly in South Africa. Many people once believed they hibernated in mud at the bottoms of ponds.

Finding Nemo, in story order.Barracuda attacks the reef: Clownfish are born male, and the dominant one can turn female if the lead female dies.
Finding Nemo, in story order.Nemo's first day of school: Real eagle rays can leap clear out of the water, which makes Mr. Ray's classroom a bit of a stretch.
Finding Nemo, in story order.A diver takes Nemo: Clownfish are among the most popular aquarium fish, and the film's success increased demand for them.
Finding Nemo, in story order.Marlin meets Dory: Dory is a blue tang, voiced by Ellen DeGeneres, who got her own sequel, Finding Dory, in 2016.
Finding Nemo, in story order.Bruce's shark meeting: Bruce is a great white shark, and his Fish are friends, not food chant mocks a shark's meetings.
Finding Nemo, in story order.The jellyfish forest: Jellyfish have no brain, heart or bones, and the group has existed for roughly 500 million years.
Finding Nemo, in story order.Riding the current with Crush: Crush is a green sea turtle riding the East Australian Current, a real current that flows along the coast of Australia.
Finding Nemo, in story order.Swallowed by a whale: Whales really do sing, and humpback songs can travel many kilometres underwater.
Finding Nemo, in story order.Nemo escapes down the drain: The dentist's office tank looks over Sydney Harbour, matching the film's Australian setting.
Finding Nemo, in story order.Father and son reunited: Marlin's journey is about a worried father learning to let go; Albert Brooks voices him.
